# sv0-gui-lib: GUI library — toolchain enablement hub

## purpose

`sv0-gui` is a planned GUI library for sv0: a platform-agnostic, deterministic
core; a versioned internal C host ABI; a headless reference adapter; and
native adapters (macOS Tahoe 26 first, then Windows, then Linux). It is a
**consumer product** like sv0-strings and sv0-mathlib. Its own repo
(`sv0-gui-lib`) does not exist yet.

The governing document is:

- `~/Documents/project-specs/sv0-gui-lib/SPEC.md`: version `0.1.34`,
  "Foundation draft for joint review", last updated 2026-08-28, audit
  baseline 2026-08-22 (meta `8a1eeb2`, sv0c `ac272be`). Decisions DG-001..034
  accepted.

This hub owns **only the toolchain side**: which sv0 language, compiler,
runtime, linker, and packaging capabilities the spec's DG-009 gates (Appendix
C, rows A1–A14, B1–B35, C1–C18) need from `sv0doc`/`sv0c`/`sv0vm`/`sv0-toolchain`,
and where each already stands. GUI-internal work (widgets, renderer, text
engine, macOS lab, notarization) belongs to the future GUI repo and is only
summarized here.

Like sv0-strings, it is SPEC-governed and **not** a toolchain milestone, so it
is absent from `task/milestone-orientation.json`.

## the spec's audit is stale (SPEC §3.1 requires revalidation)

The spec audited 2026-08-22 revisions. Since then the toolchain has shipped
several items its §4.2 lists as blocking gaps:

| SPEC §4.2 gap | State now (2026-09-27) |
|---|---|
| 1. No general host ABI (`extern`/import-symbol) | **Partly closed.** `#[extern_c] fn …;` imports, raw pointers `*const/*mut T`, and real `unsafe { }` blocks ship on the C backend; the VM rejects them with E0553 (`task/sv0c-ffi-raw-pointer-abi.Rmd`, FFI-001..015). Still missing for DG-002: symbol-name override, explicit calling convention, struct/aggregate ABI assertions, raw-pointer struct fields (FFI scope decision 2 excluded them), callbacks into sv0. |
| 2. No library/package linker contract | **Open.** `--project` is flat source concatenation with `pub` unenforced (cross-cutting stream F). The installed-toolchain manifest v1 has no dependencies (TID X-7). |
| 3. No window/event/graphics runtime | Open. By design, that is GUI adapter work over the C ABI, not compiler builtins (DG-002/§6.2 item 3). |
| 4. VM host surface fixed | Open by design (DG-008: native windowed GUI is C-backend-only through Release 0.1). |
| 5. Closures maturity-sensitive | Open. Gate C3 (deferred); DG-005 avoids closures. |
| 6. Raw pointers, RAII, Drop, Send/Sync, monomorphization, floats, slices, fn pointers unverified | **Floats:** f64 (+ i64/u64) now runs on both backends (`task/sv0c-vm-float-parity.Rmd`). **Slices:** range slices + hosted-C slice ABI shipped. **Raw pointers:** shipped (C backend). Drop, Send/Sync, fn pointers, full monomorphization are unverified. |
| 7. Global vector tables / fixed box pool | **Open.** The C runtime still has process-global tables with no per-vector release (same gap as VMX G-9). Growable tables landed (sv0c `5dce60e`) but not reclamation. |
| 8. Text insufficient | Owned by the GUI text engine (ICU4C + HarfBuzz, DG-004). The toolchain side is only B6 length-carrying buffers: the length-bearing `sv0_str` handle ABI with embedded-NUL safety has shipped. |
| 9. No accessibility bridge | GUI adapter work. |

**GUI-U01** below is the formal revalidation: it feeds a spec baseline refresh.

## toolchain readiness by DG-009 row (planning estimate, not probe evidence)

Only toolchain-owned rows are listed. `ready` = the capability exists at the
current pins and a GUI probe should pass. `partial` = exists with gaps.
`missing` = no implementation.

| Row | Capability | Toolchain readiness | Owning toolchain work |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Revision-pinned compile/link/run harness | ready (native driver, build records, `--message-format=json`) | — |
| A2 | Structs, payload enums, exhaustive match, C layout inspection | partial: language ready; no C size/align/tag assertion tooling | GUI-U03 |
| A3 | Mutable state across helpers | ready (probe needed) | — |
| A4 | Bounded sequence storage with reset/reuse | partial: `Vec` exists; no reset/reuse or capacity limit | GUI-U04 (shared with VMX-104) |
| A5 | Typed success/failure propagation | partial: enums/`match` ready; generic `Result` + `?` unverified | probe; alternative allowed |
| A6 | Q24.8/Q8.24 fixed point, checked i64, C/VM contract parity | partial: i64 on both backends; checked-arithmetic helpers are library work | probe in GUI repo |
| A7 | Application + library composition | partial: flat `--project` concat (the alternative is allowed only with a migration condition) | cross-cutting stream F; GUI-U05 |
| A8 | Bounded UTF-8 transfer with explicit length | ready-ish: length-bearing `sv0_str`, string↔byte bridges | probe |
| A10 | Deterministic core execution | ready (probe needed) | — |
| B1 | General versioned C symbol import | partial: `#[extern_c]` (no name override or calling convention) | GUI-U02 |
| B2 | Stable ABI representations (sizes, alignment, tags, handles, buffers) | missing | GUI-U03 |
| B3 | Package graph + exact lockfile + native link plan, no concatenation | missing | GUI-U05 (TID-903, stream F) |
| B4/B5/B7 | Bounded reusable allocation, deterministic release, typed exhaustion | missing (global tables, abort on exhaustion) | GUI-U04 |
| B6 | Length-carrying strings/slices/buffers | partial (strings + slices; FFI pointer+length marshalling) | GUI-U03 |
| B8 | Contract-mode consistency | ready (runtime/verified/disabled wired) | — |
| B9 | Cross-backend portable-core consistency | ready-ish (C/VM behavioral parity harness) | GUI portable core must avoid FFI types (VM E0553) |
| B10 | Sanitizers + debug across host boundary | ready (ASan/UBSan corpus, native-exe) | — |
| B11 | Stable diagnostics classes | partial (diagnostics corpus; no stable-code registry) | TID-004 registry pattern |
| C1 | f32/f64 | f64 ready on both backends; f32 unverified | — |
| C2–C7 | fn pointers, closures, generics/monomorphization, trait dispatch, Drop, Send/Sync | missing / unverified | deferred (Gate C) |
| C8 | VM host calls | missing by design | deferred |

## sequencing and a decision to take

- Nothing here preempts M5 or TID F0. GUI-U01 is cheap and useful now.
  GUI-U02..U04 are general toolchain improvements that also serve Flipper
  (E-001/E-002 ABI, RT-005) and VMX (VMX-104). Schedule them when a consumer
  is ready to probe.
- **D-1 (resolved 2026-09-27; maintainer accepted the recommendation): when does GUI Phase 0 start?** The spec
  needs a new repo, a four-role physical macOS lab (DG-024), Developer ID
  distribution, and two-person governance (DG-034). None of that is toolchain
  work, and none has an owner yet. Decision: keep GUI in **planned, not
  started** state. Run GUI-U01 now. Start the GUI repo only after TID R0 (so
  its manifest story is not built on `--project`) and GUI-U02..U04.
